title: Attention: Signal Detection Theory, Vigilance, Selective Attention
summary: Signal detection theory (SDT); vigilant observer; selective attention; saccadic eye movement; spotlight theory; overt attention.
objectives: Describe vigilant observer and vigilance decrement.
revision: SDT matrix: hit/miss/false alarm/correct rejection. Spotlight theory: attention = focused beam enhancing processing inside, reducing outside.
traps: False alarm = signal absent, say yes.
Spotlight can be covert (without eye movement).

notes.t: The vigilant observer problem concerns maintaining attention during prolonged monitoring tasks where signals are rare. Performance declines over time due to vigilance decrement.
Selective attention is the ability to focus on one stimulus while ignoring others. The cocktail party effect is a classic example: hearing your name in a noisy room.
Saccades are rapid, jerky eye movements that shift gaze from one point to another. During saccades, visual input is suppressed (saccadic suppression).
Attention is like a spotlight: processing is enhanced within the spotlight and reduced outside it. The spotlight can be moved voluntarily (overt attention) or without eye movement (covert attention).
UGC NET frequently asks about SDT outcomes (hit, miss, false alarm, correct rejection) and spotlight theory of attention.

mnemonics.title: HMFR
mnemonics.text: H — Hit (signal present, say yes), M — Miss (signal present, say no), F — False alarm (signal absent, say yes), R — Correct rejection (signal absent, say no)

flashcards.a: Attention enhances processing within a focused beam.
